edition.locus: On the Unity of the Church 25
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Haec unanimitas sub Apostolis olim fuit. Sic novus credentium populus Domini mandata custodiens, charitatem suam tenuit. Probat Scriptura divina quae dicit: Turba autem eorum qui crediderant anima et mente una agebant. Et iterum: Et erant perseverantes omnes unanimes in oratione cum mulieribus et Maria quae fuerat mater Jesu et fratribus ejus. Et ideo, quia efficacibus precibus orabant, ideo impetrare cum fiducia poterant quodcumque de Domini misericordia postulabant.
pass_a_gloss: This unanimity once was under the Apostles. Thus the new people of believers of the Lord, keeping the commands of the Lord, held their charity. Divine Scripture proves, which says: The crowd of those who had believed were acting with one soul and mind. And again: And they all were persevering, unanimous in prayer with the women and Mary, who was the mother of Jesus, and his brothers. And therefore, because they were praying with effective prayers, therefore they were able to obtain with confidence whatever they were asking from the Lord's mercy.

choices.why: credentium is a genitive plural noun

pass_b_english: This unanimity once existed under the Apostles. In this way the new people of believers, by keeping the Lord's commands, maintained their love. Divine Scripture confirms this when it says: "The whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul" (Acts 4:32). And again: "All these were constantly united in prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers" (Acts 1:14). And therefore, because they prayed with effective prayers, they were able to obtain with confidence whatever they asked from the Lord's mercy.
